messages:
sophia: heads-up — brought Halo7B (mainline checkpoint) up on int4; seeing large multilingual quality regressions on our translation benchmarks. quick numbers: en->es BLEU 28.4 (f16) -> 18.2 (int4). ppl went 11.2 -> 27.6.

ram: ouch. same tokenizer/normalizer? any changes to rotary scaling or head mapping during conversion?

sophia: same tokenizer config as float run (lexnorm=v3, byte fallback), converter used our usual int4 recipe. no manual rotary changes. i did notice an odd token normalization map for cjk + combining diacritics — some splits look different.

adele: can you paste the reproduce command + quant config?

sophia: sure — full reproduce below:
```
# reproducer
rwd-convert --src halo7b/fp16.pt --dst halo7b-int4.quant --method awq 
  --block-size 128 --symm false --calib-samples 1024

rwd-infer --model halo7b-int4.quant --task translate --src-lang en --tgt-lang es 
  --tokenizer lexnorm=v3 --rotary-scale 1.0 --max-tokens 1024 --batch 8 
```
logs:
```
INFO: running eval on wmt-mini 1000 examples
BLEU: 18.2
PPL: 27.6
Latency p50: 48ms (was 62ms fp16)
```

julian: latency improved but quality cratered. interesting that p50 dropped (good) while BLEU dropped badly. suggests numeric/embedding drift rather than kvcache ordering.

ram: could be quantization of embedding projection + tokenizer normalizer mismatch. do we have token id diffs between fp16 and int4 runs? try printing first 50 token ids for same input.

sophia: ran a small diff on one example — lots of id differences around diacritics and zero-width joiners. example: 
`el niño -> [el, 2871, 992, 345]` (fp16) vs `el niño -> [el, 2871, 9999, 345]` (int4) — so vocab mapping stayed, but normalization before tokenization differs.

adele: that smells like our conversion script reserializing tokenizer metadata (normalizer flag) or the quantized model loading a different tokenizer path. check model card and repo metadata in the artifact.

sophia: model card shows tokenizer.name = "halo-tokenizer" and normalizer = "v3". converter logs: 
```
INFO: writing artifact metadata
metadata.tokenizer: halo-tokenizer
metadata.tokenizer_normalizer: v2
```
so mismatch — converter accidentally overwrote normalizer to v2 during packaging.

ram: aha. that explains tokenization drift. but does that fully account for BLEU drop magnitude? maybe also rotary/head-scale sensitivity got amplified by AWQ int4. try re-run with explicit tokenizer override and with rotary_scale sweep.

sophia: running two quick probes now: 1) force tokenizer normalizer=v3 with current int4 artifact, 2) re-quant with metadata preserved + rotary_scale sweep [0.8, 1.0, 1.2]. posting numbers when done.

mlops-bot: job 49822 queued on rwd-infer-prod, node=gpu-a12, est 12m

benchmark-bot: started eval run 49822 (dataset=wmt-mini, examples=200)

[5m later]

sophia: probe results (200 ex sample):
- int4 (metadata fixed to v3), rotary_scale=1.0 => BLEU 25.6, PPL 14.8, latency p50 50ms
- int4 (re-quant preserving metadata), rotary_scale=1.0 => BLEU 25.9, PPL 14.2, p50 51ms
- int4 (re-quant), rotary_scale=0.8 => BLEU 26.3, PPL 13.9, p50 50ms
- fp16 baseline => BLEU 28.4, PPL 11.2, p50 62ms

julian: so majority of drop was tokenizer metadata bug (~2.8 BLEU loss), remainder likely quantization + rotary sensitivity (~1.5 BLEU). good news: we can recover most quality by: a) preserving tokenizer metadata during conversion, b) tuning rotary_scale or post-quant calibration.

adele: action items: 1) patch converter to not write tokenizer_normalizer unless explicitly changed (PR), 2) add a conversion smoke test that runs 100 multilingual samples to compare token id diffs, 3) add rotary_scale sweep as part of int4 calibs when headwise patterns appear.

ram: +1 on smoke tests. also add a quick token-id diff tool that fails conversion if >1% token mismatches on a small canonical set. will draft.

mlops-bot: job 49822 completed — artifacts uploaded: halo7b-int4-v2.quant (metadata fixed)

benchmark-bot: summary (full 1000 ex run) — halo7b-int4-v2.quant, rotary_scale=0.8 => BLEU 26.5, PPL 13.5, p50 49ms

sophia: great. will open the PRs and attach calibration sweep results + a note in the model card about recommended rotary_scale for int4 on translation. thanks all :tada:

julian: nice triage. putting follow-up on next eng-ml sync to discuss adding the token-id smoke gate to CI.

adele: fyi adding this to onboard checklist for future models — token metadata parity + calibration sweep are now required.

sophia: tagging @ram @adele for PR review once opened.
